title: Matched three-checkpoint PPO payoff matrix
method: All three matchups used the same Round402 team-preview selector and identical generated team seeds/previews within each seed set. The primary fresh set had 512 team-pair clusters and one side-swapped repeat (1,024 matches per edge); an independent earlier set had 128 clusters and two repeats. Showdown battle RNG is server-side, so the same teams/previews do not guarantee identical random battle outcomes.

team_seed_sets.purpose: independent pilot set; results showed substantial seed-set variation

point_estimate_restricted_solution.interpretation: Round465 has the highest point estimates against the other two PPO checkpoints, but the gains are below one percentage point and every cluster-bootstrap interval includes 50%. Treat this support as noise-sensitive, not as a training mixture or promotion signal.

seed_set_variability: The 128-cluster pilot favored Round464 strongly, while the 512-cluster set put all matchups near 52% for the row policy. Pooling clusters centers all edges near 50%. This makes the policy ranking sensitive to sampled teams; keep future payoff cells on shared held-out seeds and include independent seed sets.
decision: No supported difference among the three PPO checkpoints. Keep Round430 as the validated incumbent; do not claim a Nash equilibrium for VGC.
limitations: This is a restricted game with only three related PPO policies, not a full-game equilibrium certificate.
The interval resamples team-pair clusters and does not remove all variation between generated-team seed sets.
The matrix omits legal heuristic opponents and newly trained response policies.
Diagonal 50% entries are symmetry assumptions, not measured self-play results.
